clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old male accountant with no comorbidities presented in March 2020 with a 2-week history of cough and dyspnoea while working in the UK. Initial primary care assessment considered him low-risk and advised conservative management with analgesia, bed rest, and self-isolation without testing. Symptoms progressively worsened over 5 weeks, with development of pleuritic chest pain and severe cough, prompting return to Ireland and hospital admission. CT thorax/abdomen/pelvis on admission revealed a 10×11 cm anterior mediastinal mass with marked stenosis of the superior vena cava and pulmonary artery trunk, consistent with stage II disease with no distant metastases. Serum tumour markers showed markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein (17,000 ng/mL; normal 0.9–8.8 ng/mL), elevated lactate dehydrogenase (699 unit/L; normal 220–450 unit/L), and undetectable beta-hCG (<1 unit/L). Testicular examination and ultrasound were unremarkable, confirming extragonadal origin. Histological evaluation of the mediastinal lesion confirmed an extragonadal germ cell tumour of yolk sac origin. Urgent chemotherapy with the VIP regimen (etoposide, ifosfamide, cisplatin) was commenced as an inpatient with pegfilgrastim support, and the patient was discharged after completing the first of four planned cycles.
